bullets.title: NVDA: $150B buyback boost and Open Agent Safety Platform launch — bullish setup
bullets.body: NVIDIA expanded its share repurchase authorization by $150B to a total of $235B, expected to be executed through FY2028 at roughly $39B/quarter. Management cited once-in-a-generation AI demand; the buyback signals confidence at 13-14x forward P/E. Simultaneously, NVDA launched the Open Agent Safety Platform (OpenShell + Sentry on BlueField DPUs) with broad industry partners including Microsoft, Anthropic, Cisco, CrowdStrike, and Palantir. Stock +1.5-1.6% in premarket.

bullets.title: TSM: 2nm capacity ramping ahead of schedule; NVDA/AMD orders up 10-20%
bullets.body: TSMC is targeting 120k 2nm wafer starts/month by end of 2026 (vs. prior 100k target), with 140k/month in 2027 potentially achievable ahead of schedule. Major customers including AAPL, NVDA, AMD, and QCOM have raised foundry orders by an estimated 10-20%. This could drive NVDA above 70% Y/Y revenue growth for next year, with AVGO also supply-constrained on AI revenue for FY27 and upside to guidance from added capacity.

bullets.title: MRVL: Analyst Day shows path to $40-45B revenue by 2030 at mid-50s gross margin
bullets.body: UBS highlights MRVL's Analyst Day as constructive, with a credible path to ~$40-45B revenue by 2030 at mid-50s gross margins. EPS trajectory is seen in the mid-to-high teens by C'30, though guidance above $20 EPS is considered unlikely near-term. The AI custom silicon and networking story remains intact.

bullets.title: LITE: Citi raises PT to $1,400 on $11B OCS TAM opportunity
bullets.body: Citi debuted an Optical Circuit Switching TAM model estimating an ~$11B merchant opportunity by 2030, with LITE and COHR expected to capture 80%+ of wallet share. Citi raised LITE FY2027E EPS to $25 (from $23) and FY2028E to ~$41 (from $37), with OCS/UHP margins in the 60s-70s%. PT raised to $1,400 on 35x PE; COHR PT maintained at $420.

bullets.title: COHR & CSCO: Supply-constrained optical growth; CSCO targets 15% FY27 revenue growth
bullets.body: COHR is supply-constrained with demand exceeding capacity; InP capacity has quadrupled over 24 months with >50% Y/Y pro-forma growth expected in FY27 and first $3B quarterly revenue before FY27 end. Gross margin target is >42% (vs. 40.5% guidance). CSCO guided FY27 revenue +15% Y/Y driven by hyperscaler wins, Silicon One share gains, and a $100B campus switch refresh cycle; 800G ZR/ZR+ shipments exceeded 75k units.

bullets.title: CRDO: Optics could reach 30-50% of FY28 revenue with superior DSP cost structure
bullets.body: JPM ECOC recap notes CRDO optics could represent 30-50% of FY28 revenue, supported by a ~$20 DSP cost vs. ~$100 for standard solutions. The cost advantage positions CRDO competitively as hyperscalers ramp 800G/1.6T architectures. Investor sentiment described as frustrated but positively inclined toward the name.

bullets.title: MU: Earnings Wed 9/30 after close — broad buy-side conviction; PT $1,200-$1,540 range
bullets.body: Micron reports Wednesday after close with consensus EPS $31.58 on $51.14B revenue and a 6.7% implied earnings move. MS maintains OW at $1,200 PT; JPM lists $1,540 PT. Bull case: DRAM strong, NAND improving with 15-20% 4Q pricing uptake potential, <30% of bits under price-capped long-term agreements. Key debate is durability of the upcycle rather than near-term magnitude. HF community mixed but LO community remains long.

bullets.title: RBLX: Jefferies downgrades to Sell ($38 PT); Hedgeye flips to Top Long — bifurcated view
bullets.body: Jefferies cut RBLX to Underperform (from Hold) at $38 PT, arguing the recent rally is overdone and bookings trajectory too optimistic given a new algorithm limiting short-term user growth. By contrast, Hedgeye shifted from short to Top Long, citing 3Q26 as the bookings trough (guidance -14-18% Y/Y), easing comps into 2027, mobile DAU turning positive Y/Y in September, and RDC announcements including browser-playable games. Peak CCUs down -4% W/W to 27.7M but improving Y/Y vs. August.

bullets.title: META: Muse AI agent driving strong sentiment; stock +13% last week
bullets.body: META's Muse personal AI agent is seeing strong early adoption with 2,000+ connector applications including Walmart, Best Buy, and Wayfair, and remains the #1 free app in the US App Store. MS describes Muse as a credible disruptor leveraging META's consumer data advantage with near-zero take rates. Hedgeye risk range is bullish at $682-$781. OpenAI DevDay Tuesday is the next competitive read-across. META's Watermelon model expected in early October.

bullets.title: SHOP: +11% last week as Shop Pay integrated into Meta Muse — agentic commerce beneficiary
bullets.body: Shopify integrated Shop Pay into Meta's Muse Spark, enabling accelerated checkout and positioning SHOP as a direct agentic commerce beneficiary across catalog, sidekick, and UCP layers. JPM derivatives desk recommends buying SHOP November calls on a spot-up/vol-up move driven by Meta's ~4B-user ecosystem.

bullets.title: SNOW: $3.5B convertible notes offering — dilution overhang, stock -2.8% premarket
bullets.body: Snowflake launched a $3.5B convertible notes deal: $1.3B 3-year tranche (0% coupon, 52.5-57.5% conversion premium) and $2.2B 5-year tranche (0% coupon, 47.5-52.5% premium). Proceeds to fund capped calls, repurchase 2027 converts, and M&A/buybacks. Phillip Securities initiated with Buy. Stock down 2.8% in premarket on dilution concerns.

bullets.title: MSFT: Copilot ARPU upside — usage-based billing could drive 2.4x revenue/user
bullets.body: JPM estimates MSFT's new Copilot usage-based billing model (covering Cowork, Code, Autopilot agents) could drive ~2.4x revenue per user vs. seat-based pricing. GitHub Copilot usage-based pricing already accelerated revenue >60% Q/Q in June. OPCO and MS name MSFT as a top AI software winner in the ROI era, citing unmatched distribution and system-of-record positioning. Hedgeye risk range bullish at $493-$520.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Piper raises PT to $400 on Cloud upside and TPU sales formalization
bullets.body: Piper raised GOOGL PT to $400 from $395, with FY27/FY28 Cloud revenue estimates raised 15%/17% above consensus and formalized TPU sales projections above $100B by 2028. Hedgeye risk range is bearish at $334-$354, creating a notable divergence in views.

bullets.title: ANET: Buy-rated; AI Ethernet switching market seen at ~$100B by 2030 at 65% CAGR
bullets.body: Goldman maintains Buy on ANET with $225 PT; expects 3Q EPS/revenue above consensus. The AI Ethernet data center switching market is projected to reach ~$100B in 2030, growing at 65% CAGR from 2025-2030. The 650 Group upgraded campus network outlook with WLAN growing to ~$14.3B and enterprise switching to ~$30B by 2030.

bullets.title: PATH: DA Davidson downgrades to Underperform ($10 PT) on pricing pressure and AI substitution
bullets.body: DA Davidson cut PATH to Underperform with a $10 PT, citing frontier models being more cost-effective than the Maestro platform. A partner check revealed an 8-figure healthcare customer reducing spend by 25% via PowerBI/Copilot, with Workato gaining share. NNARR growth was 28% Y/Y to $73M with 60% from AI, but analyst sees downside to ASP sustainability.

bullets.title: AKAM: Buy maintained but PT cut $185→$150 on $11.6B Anthropic commitment dilution concern
bullets.body: DA Davidson maintained Buy on AKAM but cut PT from $185 to $150, viewing the $11.6B Anthropic commitment (~$5.5B capex for ~$4B EBIT) as poor capital allocation. CY26/27 EPS estimates were lowered; the deal is dilutive near-term but $14.4B in CIS commitments signed YTD are expected to be ~$4B EPS-accretive by CY29.

bullets.title: DIS: Goldman Buy-rated; F4Q26 EPS $1.73 vs $1.66 consensus; FY2027 EPS raised to $7.56
bullets.body: Goldman maintains Buy on DIS; F4Q26 EPS forecast of $1.73 beats $1.66 consensus. FY2027 EPS raised to $7.56 (+12% underlying) driven by Parks/cruise growth, Disney+ monetization, and a robust film slate. FY2027 EPS also benefits from a lower tax rate assumption.

bullets.title: FSLR: KeyBanc upgrade drives +1.3% premarket; ROTH bullish on ASP pricing power
bullets.body: FSLR was upgraded by KeyBanc, gaining 1.3% in premarket. Mizuho separately argues the ASP selloff is overdone, with pricing power sustained at high 30c/W and the stock not pricing ASPs above 33c/W. ROTH's Phil Shen met with 20+ industry experts on ITC/45X extension and module pricing dynamics. ENPH is also a confirmed participant at ROTH's Solar & Storage Symposium at RE+ (Nov 16-18).

bullets.title: BE: Mizuho notes Project Jupiter NM site on schedule; NM Supreme Court lifted air-permit stay
bullets.body: Bloom Energy's Project Jupiter New Mexico site is on schedule with the NM Supreme Court lifting the air-permit stay and federal gas pipeline review advancing toward a December decision. Mizuho maintains constructive view on BE.

bullets.title: AMPL: DA Davidson bullish ahead of 3Q; data ingestion >30%, NRR +9pts to 105%
bullets.body: DA Davidson is bullish on AMPL heading into 3Q, seeing upside to 21% consensus revenue growth. Data ingestion is growing >30%, NRR improved +9 points to 105%, and the Statsig integration is delivering 20-30% per-product uplift. Analyst sees potential for 20-25%+ growth sustainability.
